name: @markforge/adapters-ocr
description: Scanned pages to IR: pluggable recognizers, tesseract.js by default, confidence into provenance
optionalDependenciesComment: tesseract.js is optional and lazily imported: it is a WASM bundle plus a language model that has to be fetched, so an install must not depend on it and a Markdown conversion must not load it. See docs/adr/0017-ocr-recognizer-boundary.md.

markforge.note: Eager, and ADR-0015 said deferred. Measured: core and browser reach only documentFromPages, which is a pure function over already-recognised pages, and tree-shaking leaves tesseract.js out of both — the recogniser is injected (ADR-0017). This package bundled ALONE does contain tesseract.js, because its entry re-exports createTesseractRecognizer, and that is legitimate: someone importing that symbol wants it. The heavy-artifact rule therefore applies to the shipped browser entry point, not to every package standalone.
